angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 730,485 km at 66.03 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.1439 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 66.03 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.05 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Pearson et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 80606 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..178P/abstract): 730,485 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.05 solar masses from Pearson et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 80606 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..178P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5565 K from Pearson et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 80606 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..178P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Pearson et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 80606 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..178P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-80606.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.417, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
